knowledge_point.title: Determining the Dimension of the Product of Two Matrices

question.:question/problem:
Let
$A=\begin{bmatrix}-4 & -3 \\ -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 3\end{bmatrix}$
and
$B=\begin{bmatrix}-4 & -3 \\ -2 & -1\end{bmatrix}$.
Then, the dimensions of $AB$ are {{field-1}} $\times$ {{field-2}}.

For conformable factors, use the number of rows of the first factor and the number of columns of the second.
question.:question/worked-solution:
We notice that $A$ is a $4\times 2$ matrix and $B$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix. 

There are $2$ columns in $A$ and $2$ rows in $B.$ Since the number of columns in $A$ equals the number of rows in $B,$ the matrices $A$ and $B$ are conformable for multiplication. 

The product $AB$ has dimensions $4\times 2:$

$$
{A}_{4\times \boxed{\text{2}}}{\times }_{✓}{B}_{\boxed{\text{2}}\times 2}={AB}_{4\times 2}
$$
